extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in arithmetic geometry and number theory (readers of Mochizuki/IUT-related work)
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, reductions, and technical lemmas from Section 1 of a research article (Go Yamashita) reducing the main theorem (an inequality related to the abc conjecture) to p-adic log-volume and multiradial inequalities used in IUT. Includes arithmetic-geometric setup, height functions, log-different/log-conductor, and local p-adic lemmas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topology on automorphism groups for compact G
rubrics_metrics.description: When G is a compact Hausdorff topological group, equip Aut(G) with the compact-open topology and Inn(G), Out(G) with the induced topology. If H is a topological group and f is a continuous homomorphism, equip Out_G(H) with the induced topology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the topological conventions used when discussing automorphism groups in later arguments; no scoring guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of UP1 and tripod over K
rubrics_metrics.description: For a field K, write UP1 := P^1_K  {0,1,∞}g. An algebraic curve over K isomorphic to P^1_K minus three points is called a tripod over K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes the basic one-dimensional hyperbolic object (projective line minus three points) used for reductions (Belyi maps to UP1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyperbolic orbicurve over k
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is a generically scheme-like algebraic stack over a field k which has a finite étale Galois covering Y → X, where Y is a hyperbolic curve over a finite extension of k, then X is called a hyperbolic orbicurve over k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This identifies the class of stacks/curves to which the Diophantine inequalities are applied; used to reduce statements to hyperbolic curve cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cyclotome and cyclotomic characters
rubrics_metrics.description: For a field K of characteristic 0 and a separable closure Kbar, define bZ(K) := Hom(Q/Z, Kbar^×) and Q/Z(K) := bZ(K) ⊗_{bZ} Q/Z; similarly Z_l(K) and Z/nZ(K). A cyclotome associated to K is any of these with the natural continuous Gal(Kbar/K)-action. Write cyc = cyc;K and cyc;l = cyc;l;K for the (l-adic) cyclotomic character of Gal(Kbar/K).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fixes notation and objects (cyclotomes, cyclotomic characters) used later in Galois/action arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arithmetic line bundle and APic(X)
rubrics_metrics.description: An arithmetic line bundle on X is a pair L = (L, ||·||_L) where L is a line bundle on X and ||·||_L is a hermitian metric on the associated analytic line bundle on X(C) compatible with complex conjugation. Morphisms are bundle morphisms respecting metrics. APic(X) denotes isomorphism classes of arithmetic line bundles (group under tensor product) and pullback maps f^*: APic(Y) → APic(X) for morphisms f: X→Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes the arithmetic-geometric objects used to define heights; emphasizes metric data and functoriality under pullback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arithmetic divisor, principal arithmetic divisor, ADiv(F) and degree maps
rubrics_metrics.description: For a number field F, an arithmetic divisor (resp. R-arithmetic divisor) is a finite formal sum a = ∑_{v∈V(F)} c_v v with c_v ∈ Z (resp. c_v ∈ R) for non-Archimedean v and c_v ∈ R for Archimedean v. Support and eﬀectivity defined as usual. Principal arithmetic divisors arise from non-zero f∈F via valuations and Archimedean contributions. ADiv(F) (resp. ADiv_R(F)) denote groups; there is a natural isomorphism ADiv(F)/(principal) ≅ APic(Spec O_F). A (non-normalised) degree map deg_F : APic(Spec O_F) ≅ ADiv(F)/(principal) → R is defined by sending v (non-arch) to log(q_v) and v (arch) to 1. Normalised degree [F:Q]^{-1} deg_F is invariant under finite extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives the divisor/degree formalism needed to compute heights and log-different/log-conductor. Important for defining normalized heights and comparing across extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Height function ht_L and its properties
rubrics_metrics.description: For an arithmetic line bundle L on X, define the (logarithmic) height ht_L : X(Q) → R by ht_L(x) := (1/[F:Q]) deg_F(x^* L) for x ∈ X(F) (x^* is pullback to Spec O_F). Properties: ht_{L1⊗L2} = ht_{L1} + ht_{L2}; for L with ample generic fibre and some tensor power generated by global sections, ht_L is bounded below (ht_L & 0) and the bounded discrepancy class of ht_L depends only on L_Q.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the precise normalization and boundedness facts used repeatedly in Diophantine inequalities and reduction steps; includes argument sketch using sections and Archimedean/non-Archimedean contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bounded discrepancy class notation and equivalence
rubrics_metrics.description: For functions φ,ψ : X(Q) → R, write φ & ψ (resp. φ . ψ, |φ−ψ| < C) if φ(x) > ψ(x) + C (resp. φ(x) < ψ(x) + C, |φ(x)−ψ(x)| < C) for some constant C and all x. An equivalence class of functions under bounded discrepancy is a bounded discrepancy class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to express height equality up to additive bounded error; central to arguments where only class matters (ht_{L_Q} notation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Log-different function log-diﬀ_X
rubrics_metrics.description: For x ∈ X(Q) with minimal field of definition F, the different ideal of F determines an effective arithmetic divisor d_x; define log-diﬀ_X(x) := (1/[F:Q]) deg_F(d_x) ∈ R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This local-global different measure is used in Diophantine inequalities; note: log-diﬀ_X depends only on the scheme X_Q.

rubrics_metrics.name: Log-conductor function log-cond_D
rubrics_metrics.description: For an effective Cartier divisor D ⊂ X and UX := X  ackslash D, for x ∈ UX(Q) with minimal field F, let D_x be the pullback divisor to Spec O_F and fD_x := (D_x)_red; define log-cond_D(x) := (1/[F:Q]) deg_F(fD_x) ∈ R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depends on the pair (X,D) as Z-schemes, but the bounded discrepancy class on UX(Q) depends only on (X_Q, D_Q). Used alongside log-diﬀ in inequalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compact domain and compactly bounded subsets KV
rubrics_metrics.description: A non-empty compact subset of a topological space is a compact domain if it is the closure of its interior. For X normal, Z-proper, Z-flat, UX open dense, choose finite V ⊂ V(Q) containing all archimedean places in support; for each v choose a Gal(Q_v/Q_v)-stable compact domain K_v ⊂ UX(Q_v) (or its analogue for Archimedean). Then KV UX(Q) denotes the set of rational points x ∈ UX(Q) with all conjugates contained in the chosen K_v; such KV is called a compactly bounded subset and V its support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This concept is used to localize Diophantine arguments to subsets with good local bounds (compactness important for limiting arguments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 1.1: comparison of log-different and log-conductor under finite maps
rubrics_metrics.description: Let f: Y → X be a generically finite morphism of normal, Z-proper, Z-flat schemes of dimension two. Let D ⊂ X, E ⊂ Y be effective Z-flat Cartier divisors with (a) D_Q, E_Q reduced, (b) E_Q = f_Q^{-1}(D_Q)_red, (c) f_Q restricts to a finite étale morphism (UY)_Q → (UX)_Q where UX := X ackslash D and UY := Y ackslash E. Then (1) log-diﬀ_X ∘ j_Y + log-cond_D ∘ j_Y . log-diﬀ_Y + log-cond_E on UY(Q). (2) If additionally (d) the ramification index of f_Q at each point of E_Q divides e, then log-diﬀ_Y . log-diﬀ_X ∘ j_Y + (1−1/e) log-cond_D ∘ j_Y on UY(Q).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof sketch: reduce to finite tamely ramified morphism outside a finite set S, use properties of diﬀerents and control S-portion by a local claim about p-adic diﬀerents: for fixed p and degree bound d there is n so that for Galois extensions L/K of degree ≤ d the diﬀerent contains p^n O_L. These inequalities are used to compare global log-quantities after pullback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 1.2: reduction to inequality on UP1
rubrics_metrics.description: Fix finite V_non ⊂ V_non and a compactly bounded KV ⊂ UP1(Q) with support V = V_non ∪ V_arc. Then to prove Theorem 0.1 it suffices to show: for any d∈Z_{>0} and ε>0, ht_{O(1)}^{P1 ackslash{0,1,∞}} . (1+ε)(log-diﬀ_{P1} + log-cond_{0,1,∞}) on KV ∩ UP1(Q)^{(≤d)}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses existence of finite étale coverings Y→X with controlled ramification indices, pulling back heights and applying Lemma 1.1; then reduces general X to the tripod/P^1 minus three points case via Belyi maps and compactness arguments. Guidance includes how to choose coverings with large ramification index to force inequalities and use of natural isomorphisms of line bundles.

rubrics_metrics.name: First reduction: sufficing to consider D = ∅ and strategy outline
rubrics_metrics.description: Using covers Y→X and Lemma 1.1, one can reduce the main inequality to the case D = ∅ (i.e., no removed divisor) and argue by contradiction using compactness to produce sequences converging locally and then applying Belyi maps f: X → P^1 unramified over UP1 to reduce to UP1-case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains the high-level reduction plan: pullback to hyperbolic Y with controlled ramification, choose ε′ so that (1+ε′)^2 < 1+ε, and derive contradiction if inequality fails; uses bounds relating heights, log-different, and log-conductor and degree comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 1.3: p-adic inclusions for log of second-order unit group
rubrics_metrics.description: Let k be a finite extension of Q_p with ramification index e. Define integers a,b by explicit formulas depending on p and e (given in the lemma). Then p^a O_k ⊆ log_p(O_k^{(2)}) ⊆ p^b O_k. If further p>2 and e ≤ p−2, then equalities hold: p^a O_k = log_p(O_k^{(2)}) = p^b O_k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses embedding into C_p, the p-adic exponential map, Kummer theory in the totally ramified p-power extension reduction, and explicit valuation computations. These bounds are used later in volume/log-shell estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 1.4: tensor-product normalization inclusion with diﬀerent
rubrics_metrics.description: For a finite set {k_i}_{i∈I} of finite extensions of Q_p and fixed element (·)∈I, with d_i = d_{k_i/Q_p}, set d_I = ∑_{i∈I ackslash{(·)}} d_i. Then p^{d_I((⊗_i O_{k_i})^{nor})} ⊆ (⊗_i O_{k_i})^{nor} ⊆ (⊗_i O_{k_i})^{nor} with appropriate normalization: more precisely, pd_I(·) ((⊗_i O_{k_i})^{nor}) ⊆ (⊗_i O_{k_i})^{nor}, and the displayed inclusions in the lemma hold (see text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical algebraic-integral statement about normalization of tensor products of integer rings and powers of p; used to control denominators/indices in later module manipulations. Proof reduces to #I=2 and uses properties of the different ideal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 1.5: inequalities for differents under extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Let k⊃k0 be finite extensions of Q_p with ramification indices e,e0 and differents d_k,d_{k0}. Let m be unique integer with p^m || [k:k0]. Then (1) d_{k0} + 1/e0 ≤ d_k + 1/e, with equality if k/k0 is tamely ramified. (2) If k is a finite Galois extension of a tamely ramified extension of k0 then d_k ≤ d_{k0} + m + 1/e0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives quantitative comparisons of differents when passing to extensions and when there are p-power degree contributions; used to control local contributions to log-different under extensions and in Lemma 1.6 arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remark: necessity of log-cond term under extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: The quantity 'log-diﬀ + log-cond' (not just log-diﬀ alone) behaves well under passage to field extensions; this is one rationale for the appearance of log-cond in Diophantine inequalities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains conceptual reason for pairing log-different with log-conductor in global inequalities—important for correct functorial behavior under base change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Log-volume functions and normalization
rubrics_metrics.description: For finite extension k/Q_p, define log_k for the (non-normalised) log-volume (log of usual p-adic measure) on compact open subsets and normalised version so that log_k(e O_k) = 1 for a CAF. The normalised log-volume serves as a local analogue of deg_F. For tensor products of extensions, sums of normalised log-volumes give a log-volume function on compact opens of the tensor product, normalized so log((⊗ O_{k_i})) = 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These local log-volume notions are introduced to translate global degree/height computations to local p-adic volume calculations used in later inter-universal Teichmüller arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 1.6: bounds for automorphisms of tensor product of integer rings and log-volumes
rubrics_metrics.description: Let {k_i}_{i∈I} be finite extensions of Q_p with ramification indices e_i, and define integers a_i,b_i from Lemma 1.3, d_I = ∑ d_i, a_I = ∑ a_i, b_I = ∑ b_i. For an automorphism θ of the Z_p-module (⊗_i O_{k_i})^{nor} extended Q_p-linearly, write I_{>p^2} = {i | e_i > p^2}. Then for any integer r≥1 and i0∈I one has an inclusion of the form θ(p^{r} (⊗ O_{k_i})^{nor}) ⊆ p^{⌊b(r,d_I,a_I)⌋} (⊗ O_{k_i})^{nor} with explicit exponents involving b, d_I, a_I. Moreover, the normalized log-volume satisfies an upper bound: log_{k_I}(p^{...}((⊗ O_{k_i})^{nor})) ≤ ((p−1)+d_I+1) log p + ∑_{i∈I_{>p^2}} (3+log(e_i)). In the special case p>2 and all e_i=1, exact equalities and the vanishing log-volume on the unit tensor appear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical control of how Z_p-module automorphisms distort p-adic denominators and how that affects the normalized local log-volume; crucial for the later 'inequality j log(q) j ... j log(...) j' reductions. Proof combines Lemmas 1.3–1.5 and explicit combinatorial estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Log-shell I_k and holomorphic hull
rubrics_metrics.description: For a non-Archimedean local field or CAF k, define I_k := (unit ball) (denoted as 'log-shell'). For v_1,...,v_n places over v_Q, write I_{v1;...;vn} := ⊗_{i} I_{F_{v_i}} under tensor products taken over Q_{p(v_Q)}. For a subset A inside such an I, its holomorphic hull is the smallest subset containing A of the form ⊕_{i} a_i O_{L_i} with a_i ∈ O_{L_i} in the direct sum decomposition of the topological fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines concrete compact sets (log-shells) in tensor products and a notion of holomorphic hull used when tracking images of local compact domains under automorphisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primitive automorphisms subgroup Aut(C)^{prim}
rubrics_metrics.description: Define Aut(C)^{prim} ⊂ Aut(C) to be the subgroup generated by complex conjugation and multiplication by primitive 4-th roots of unity (i.e., by complex conjugation and multiplication by ±1, ±i); Aut(C)^{prim} ≅ Z/4Z ⋊ {±1}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fixes a restricted subgroup of field automorphisms for use in descent/compatibility issues when working with archimedean embeddings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial tuple data (F, E_F, V_bad_mod, l, V) conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose tuple (F, E_F, V_bad_mod, l, V) with: (1) F a number field with 1/2 ∈ F and Fbar algebraic closure fixed; (2) E_F an elliptic curve over F with Aut_F(E_F)={±1}, whose 2·3·5-torsion points are rational over F, and F is Galois over its field of moduli F_mod; (3) non-empty finite V_bad_mod ⊂ V_mod such that for v∈V_bad_mod, E_F has bad multiplicative reduction at corresponding places; (4) prime l≥5 prime to elements of V_bad_mod and to ord_w(q-parameters) of E_F at bad places; (5) finite V ⊂ V(K) where K := F(E_F[l]) mapping bijectively to V_mod under restriction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the 'initial (2)-data' ingredients (not yet full initial data) specifying the global arithmetic setup for the IUT constructions and later volume/log computations; each condition is used to control torsion, reduction type, and Galois properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 1.7: properties of the chosen elliptic curve and fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Given the above initial choices: (1) F_{tpd} := F_mod(E_{F_mod}[2]) is independent of choice of model E_{F_mod}; (2) E_F has at most semistable reduction at all non-archimedean places; (3) any model of E_F with 3-torsion rational over F is isomorphic to E_F over F; in particular there is an isomorphism E_{F_{tpd}} ≅ E_F over F for a model over F_{tpd} with F ⊃ F_{tpd}(E_{tpd}[3]); (4) the extension K ⊃ F_mod is Galois.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collects field and model properties that will be required for later Galois/ramification/coordinate arguments; proof sketched via automorphism sequence and torsion rationality.
